result.title: Whose Values, Which Contexts, and What Signals? Grounding Cultural Value Alignment with Re3Culture
result.summary: Cultural value alignment requires not only model optimization but also a well-specified target grounded in real-human evidence. Yet how such targets should be grounded in human data remains largely unexplored, raising three fundamental questions: (1) whose values should be represented? (2) where should cultural values be observed? and (3) what signals reveal underlying values? We investigate these questions through Re3Culture, a large-scale dataset linking (i) Representative communities: 700+ human participants across four cultures recruited through cultural-affiliation screening and demographic-aware sampling; (ii) Realistic scenario: culturally sensitive scenarios selected by community members, e.g., family and kinship; and (iii) Revealed value signals: 1,400+ value surveys, 20,000+ topic-grounded behavioral principles and explicit value priorities with responses for 6,000+ situated questions. Our analysis shows why these choices matter for defining the target, with three implications. First, estimating cultural values requires both community affiliation and broad internal coverage. Substituting other cultures or restricting subgroup coverage shifts value estimates. LLM simulations also disproportionately reflect particular subgroups. Second, values must be observed in concrete, community-guided situations. Abstract questionnaire profiles weakly recover situated priorities, and communities differ in which scenarios they identify as culturally value-revealing. Third, value priorities should be elicited explicitly, not learned from response preferences or bottom-line answers alone. Preferences conflate value agreement with other response-level qualities, and similar answers can be derived from different value priorities. By addressing these requirements, Re3Culture provides the first human-grounded resource that explicitly informs target definition for cultural value alignment.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建 Re3Culture 数据集，以 700 余名跨四种文化的参与者、社区选定的情境场景和显式价值优先序问卷，讨论文化价值对齐的目标应如何在真实人类数据上被界定，并分析"代表谁、在哪观察、用何种信号"三类选择对估计结果的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心观察——仅由回答偏好等行为信号难以反推内在价值优先序，相似输出可能源于不同内部状态——与 LVR 中仅用答案监督难以约束 latent 推理状态、需显式获取内部信号的困境结构相似，可作为"显式状态监督 vs 行为监督"的问题表述线索供核查，但领域相距较远，与视觉或多模态推理无直接联系。
